working: Na/liq. NH3 reduces the alkyne to the trans-alkene, so L is trans-PhCH=CHCH3. Lindlar's catalyst gives the cis-alkene, so K is cis-PhCH=CHCH3. K and L are therefore geometrical isomers. Ionic HBr addition to K goes through the benzylic carbocation, giving M = PhCHBrCH2CH3. Peroxide (radical) HBr addition to L goes through the benzylic radical, giving N = PhCH2CHBrCH3. M and N are position isomers, not stereoisomers or geometrical isomers. Only option 1 is correct.
